core_obligations: Let S' be the quotient of the base change by its b-power torsion and note that the natural map to the blowup algebra is surjective, since b becomes a nonzerodivisor there (proof lines 17409-17417).
Construct an inverse: send an element y/b^n with y in J^n, written as a finite sum of x_i s_i with x_i in I^n, to the class of the sum of s_i tensor x_i/a^n (proof lines 17418-17421).
Check well-definedness using that an element of the kernel of the map from S tensor I^n to J^n is annihilated by a^n and hence dies in the torsion quotient (proof lines 17422-17423).
proof_roadmap: Get surjectivity onto the blowup algebra and identify the torsion obstruction (proof lines 17408-17417).
Build the inverse map on fractions and verify it is well defined via the torsion condition (proof lines 17418-17424).
difficulty_reason: For a ring map from R to S, an ideal I and a in I with image b, the lemma identifies the blowup algebra of S at b with the quotient of the base-changed blowup algebra by the elements annihilated by a power of b (statement lines 17400-17406). The proof does not construct a natural isomorphism from universal properties: it defines the target quotient, gets surjectivity because b is a nonzerodivisor in the blowup algebra, and then builds the inverse map explicitly on fractions, checking well-definedness against the kernel of the map from S tensor I^n to J^n, where the torsion condition is exactly what is needed (proof lines 17408-17424). Locating well-definedness in the torsion quotient is the content of the argument. H2.
